usefulness.evidence: The break-even return with a tax-on-gains input answers 'pay off or invest' with the reader's own numbers: 7.19% at 6.5% with 15% tax, 3.40% at a 3% mortgage, 6.70% with no tax. The site's guide and comparison give only fixed pre-tax examples, so this adds a decision threshold rather than restating sources.

sourceAndAssumptions.evidence: IRS Publication 936 itemizing condition verified live (HTTP 200); steady-return, same-cash, tax-at-end and P&I-only assumptions are stated on the page and in the tool; the 7% return and 15% tax are labelled placeholders, not forecasts.

conditionsAndCounterexample.evidence: Replay of calc.py is byte-identical to output.json (canonical sha 8f2ad54d...), including its built-in assertion that 0% tax break-even equals the effective annual rate (6.697% at 6.5%, 3.042% at 3%). TS engine matches all 7 cases (0 mismatches) and the 0%-tax break-even equals (1+APR/12)^12-1 to 1e-9. Boundaries: $0 extra returns null break-even and the UI says 'Enter an extra amount to compare'; 0% mortgage gives 0.00% break-even; 3% mortgage flips to investing (+$116,226.56). Limitation recorded: break-even bisection is capped at 30%, so 100% tax or a mortgage rate near 27%+ displays 30.00% instead of 'no break-even/above 30%' (advisory, unrealistic inputs).

renderedConsistency.evidence: Round 2 render (snapshot 4a3caa54...) matches the analysis: default ($8,188 ahead, 7.19%, $322,599, $314,410, $135,115, 9 years 2 months) and all prose/FAQ figures match output.json; the new FAQ 6 figure ($72,807.70 at 5%) is output.json case 2. Final rendered review of this route: PASS.
